facts: Official Branding with Type page identifies Bw Gradual as a current Branding with Type family.
Official foundry release identifies Alberto Romanos as designer and states seven weights with matching oblique italics.
Official foundry material states support for all European Latin languages.

license.note: Branding with Type sells an all-in-one commercial license and a separate demo license. Exact ONOD capability mapping remains pending; the recovered Open Source label is invalid.

facts: Official Branding with Type page identifies Bw Modelica and Alberto Romanos as designer.
Official page lists eight weights with matching oblique italics for the standard width and a larger four-width collection.
Official page states the standard-width character set was expanded from European Latin to Greek and Cyrillic, with an LGC subset explicitly listed.

license.note: Branding with Type commercial licensing applies; exact ONOD capability mapping remains pending and the recovered Open Source label is invalid.

facts: Official Branding with Type collection page explicitly describes Bw Nista as a font family designed by Alberto Romanos.
Official page lists three Bw Nista subfamilies and seven named weights with matching oblique italics in each.
Official page states support for all European Latin languages / Extended Latin.

license.note: Branding with Type commercial licensing applies; exact ONOD capability mapping remains pending and the recovered Open Source label is invalid.

facts: Official Indian Type Foundry page identifies Duplet as an Indian Type Foundry family designed by Diana Ovezea and Rafał Buchner.
Official page lists 14 styles across seven named weights with companion italics.
Official page describes the family as covering European languages written with the Latin script and exposes retail buying options.

license.note: The official foundry sells Duplet under retail licensing. The recovered generic Open Source label is invalid; an exact ONOD capability policy remains pending until ITF license terms are normalized.

facts: Official Fontfabric page identifies Gilam as a Fontfabric family designed by Plamen Motev and Ivan Petrov.
Official page lists 18 font styles and paid Desktop/Web/App/Epub/Digital Ads licensing options.
Official page explicitly states support for Extended Latin, Cyrillic and Greek alphabets.

license.note: Fontfabric exposes multiple paid license classes rather than a single open-source license id. Exact capability mapping stays pending until the applicable Fontfabric EULA is normalized.

facts: Official TypeMates page identifies Gratimo Grotesk and Jakob Runge / Mona Franz as designers.
Official page specifies 12 styles and six weights.
Official page states support for 270+ languages across Latin, Cyrillic and Greek.

license.note: TypeMates commercial license/EULA capability policy is not yet normalized in ONOD.

facts: Official WELTKERN typeface page identifies Lausanne as a current WELTKERN family.
Official WELTKERN licensing/credit material identifies TWK Lausanne as designed by Nizar Kazan and published by WELTKERN.

license.note: WELTKERN exposes commercial licensing, but the recovered generic Open Source label must not be replaced by a definitive ONOD license id until the exact family/license terms are normalized into a reviewed policy.

facts: Official DOT COLON Nacelle page identifies Nacelle Version 1.00 and its named styles.
Official DOT COLON site identifies Sora Sagano as Type Designer.
Official Nacelle page explicitly states that Nacelle is licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1.
Official Newlyn page identifies New Spirit as a current Newlyn commercial serif family and Windsor revival.
Official page lists six Roman styles from Light through Heavy and additional Italic/Condensed/Compressed families.
Official tester exposes English, Spanish, German, French, Polish, Italian and Hungarian, establishing Latin-script support.

license.note: Newlyn sells direct commercial/self-hosted web licensing. Exact ONOD capability mapping remains pending; the recovered Open Source label is invalid.

facts: Official designer product page identifies Nohemi as a Rajesh Rajput typeface.

license.note: Identity is primary-source verified; exact redistribution/self-hosting/download license terms remain unresolved and must stay pending.

facts: Official Displaay page identifies Saans as a Displaay family designed by Martin Vácha.
Official page lists Saans as a 12-style proportional family within the Saans collection and explicitly exposes a variable font with Weight, Slant and Mono axes.
Official support section lists Latin character sets and Latin-script languages.

license.note: Displaay sells retail licenses and free full trials; the recovered generic Open Source label is invalid. Exact Displaay EULA capability mapping remains pending.

facts: Official creator page states that Vercetti Regular is also known as Vercetti and identifies Richard Mandona as Typeface Designer and Filippos Fragkogiannis as Creative Director.

Official page states the font is distributed under Licence Amicale and references Licence Amicale V.0.2 while imposing additional EULA restrictions; ONOD therefore keeps the normalized license policy pending until those terms are reconciled.
Official supported-language list contains Latin-script languages and no Cyrillic/Greek set.

license.note: The official page names Licence Amicale V.0.2, but its page-specific EULA also restricts modification/public file sharing. ONOD will not map capabilities until a reviewed policy reconciles both sources.
